questions.stem: A small group of birds colonizes an island, and an allele rare on the mainland becomes common there. What explains this?

options.why: Allele frequencies changed.
This is chance, not selection.
Correct. A few founders carried, by chance, a different set of alleles.
Gene flow would make populations more similar.

questions.explanation: A few founders carried, by chance, a different set of alleles.

questions.stem: Two cube-shaped cells have side lengths of 3 µm and 7 µm. Which statement correctly compares their surface area-to-volume ratios?

options.text: The 3 µm cell has a ratio of 2, which is greater than the 7 µm cell's 0.86, so it exchanges materials more efficiently
options.why: Correct. For a cube, SA:V = 6s²/s³ = 6/s.

options.text: The 3 µm cell has a ratio of 2, which is greater, so it exchanges materials less efficiently
options.why: A greater ratio means more surface per unit volume: more efficient exchange.

options.text: Both cells have the same ratio, 6, because both are cubes
options.why: The ratio depends on side length.

options.text: The 7 µm cell has the greater ratio, 42, so it exchanges materials more efficiently
options.why: SA:V decreases as size increases.

questions.explanation: SA:V = 6/s: 2 for 3 µm and 0.86 for 7 µm. Smaller cells have more surface area per unit volume.

questions.stem: Plants often form new species within a single area when errors in meiosis double their chromosome number. This is:

options.why: Correct. Polyploids are reproductively isolated from the parent species.
That produces similar traits in unrelated species.
Gene flow prevents speciation.
No geographic barrier is involved.

questions.explanation: Polyploids are reproductively isolated from the parent species.

questions.stem: Two populations of frogs live in the same pond but breed in different months. What type of barrier is this?

options.why: Correct. They are separated by breeding time.
No hybrids form.
They live in the same place.
Their parts are not the issue.

questions.explanation: They are separated by breeding time.

questions.stem: A circular plasmid of 4000 base pairs is cut by a restriction enzyme at positions 1800 and 3500. The fragments are separated by gel electrophoresis. Which bands appear, and which travels farthest?

options.text: 1800 bp, 1700 bp and 500 bp; the 500 bp band travels farthest
options.why: A circular plasmid cut twice gives two fragments, not three.
The plasmid is cut into pieces.

options.text: 1700 bp and 2300 bp; the 2300 bp band travels farthest
options.why: Smaller fragments move through the gel more easily.

options.text: 1700 bp and 2300 bp; the 1700 bp band travels farthest
options.why: Correct. Two cuts in a circle give two pieces; smaller fragments move farther.

questions.explanation: The fragments are 3500 − 1800 = 1700 bp and 4000 − 1700 = 2300 bp.

questions.stem: Which modification of eukaryotic pre-mRNA allows one gene to code for more than one protein?

options.why: Correct. Different exon combinations make different mRNAs.
That copies DNA.
The cap protects the mRNA.
The tail aids stability and export.

questions.explanation: Different exon combinations make different mRNAs.

questions.stem: The producers in an ecosystem store 10,000 kcal of energy. Assuming about 10% transfer between trophic levels, about how much energy is available to the secondary consumers?

options.why: Count the number of transfers from producers.
About 10% is passed on; about 90% is lost.
Count the number of transfers from producers.
Correct. 2 transfers of 10% each.

questions.explanation: Each level keeps about 10%: 10,000 × 0.1^2 = 100 kcal.

questions.stem: A linear nucleic acid strand made of 263 nucleotides is completely hydrolyzed. How many water molecules are consumed?

options.why: Correct. A chain of 263 monomers has 262 bonds, and each bond involves one water molecule.
There is one fewer bond than monomers in a linear chain.
There is one fewer bond than monomers.
Each bond involves one water molecule, not two.

questions.explanation: Linking 263 monomers forms 262 bonds; each is broken using one water molecule.

questions.stem: A diploid cell has 46 chromosomes (2n = 46). How many chromatids are present in the cell during metaphase of mitosis?

options.why: Mitosis does not halve the chromosome number.
Check whether DNA has been replicated at this point.
Correct. After S phase each chromosome has two sister chromatids.
Replication doubles the chromatids only once.

questions.explanation: 46 chromosomes; chromatid count is 92 in metaphase of mitosis.

questions.stem: Two cube-shaped cells have side lengths of 3 µm and 9 µm. Which statement correctly compares their surface area-to-volume ratios?

options.text: Both cells have the same ratio, 6, because both are cubes
options.why: The ratio depends on side length.

options.text: The 9 µm cell has the greater ratio, 54, so it exchanges materials more efficiently
options.why: SA:V decreases as size increases.

options.text: The 3 µm cell has a ratio of 2, which is greater than the 9 µm cell's 0.67, so it exchanges materials more efficiently
options.why: Correct. For a cube, SA:V = 6s²/s³ = 6/s.

options.text: The 3 µm cell has a ratio of 2, which is greater, so it exchanges materials less efficiently
options.why: A greater ratio means more surface per unit volume: more efficient exchange.

questions.explanation: SA:V = 6/s: 2 for 3 µm and 0.67 for 9 µm. Smaller cells have more surface area per unit volume.

questions.stem: Which is the best measure of an organism's evolutionary fitness?

options.why: Strength does not define fitness.
Longevity matters only if it increases reproduction.

options.text: The number of its offspring that survive to reproduce
options.why: Correct. Fitness is reproductive success.
Size does not define fitness.

questions.explanation: Fitness is reproductive success.

questions.stem: A sample of double-stranded DNA is 18% cytosine. What percentage of the bases are adenine?

options.why: 18% is the amount of guanine, which pairs with cytosine.
Correct. guanine also makes up 18%; the remaining 64% is split equally between the other two bases.
That is the total for both remaining bases together.
Both members of each base pair must be accounted for.

questions.explanation: By base pairing, cytosine = guanine = 18%. The other two bases share 64%, so each is 32%.

questions.stem: One strand of DNA reads 5′-CTCCGACG-3′. What is the sequence of the complementary strand, written 5′ to 3′?

options.why: Correct. Pair each base and reverse the direction, because strands are antiparallel.
The complementary strand is antiparallel; written 5′ to 3′ it is reversed.
Each base must be paired, not just reversed.
DNA contains T, not U.

questions.explanation: The complement of 5′-CTCCGACG-3′ is 3′-GAGGCTGC-5′, written 5′-CGTCGGAG-3′.

questions.stem: Bacteria release a signaling molecule and begin forming a biofilm only when the population is dense. What is this called?

options.why: That is programmed cell death.
That is cell division.
That uses hormones in animals.
Correct. Signals accumulate to a threshold at high density.

questions.explanation: Signals accumulate to a threshold at high density.

questions.stem: Red and white snapdragons produce pink offspring. What pattern of inheritance is this?

options.why: Not related to sex chromosomes.
One gene with two alleles explains it.
Correct. The heterozygote is intermediate.
Both traits would appear fully.

questions.explanation: The heterozygote is intermediate.

questions.stem: A plant cell has a water potential of -0.79 MPa. It is placed in a solution with a water potential of -1.1 MPa. Which describes the net movement of water?

options.text: Out of the cell, because water moves toward higher water potential
options.why: Water moves toward lower water potential.

options.text: No net movement, because water potential does not affect osmosis
options.why: Differences in water potential drive osmosis.

options.text: Into the cell, because the cell has the higher water potential
options.why: Water moves from higher to lower water potential.

options.text: Out of the cell, because water moves toward the lower (more negative) water potential
options.why: Correct. Water moves from -0.79 MPa to -1.1 MPa.

questions.explanation: Water flows from higher to lower water potential: from the cell into the solution.

questions.stem: An organism has a diploid number of 10. Ignoring crossing over, how many genetically different gametes can it produce by independent assortment?

options.why: Combinations multiply: each pair has 2 orientations.
The count is 2 raised to the number of pairs.
Correct. With 5 homologous pairs, there are 2^5 combinations.
The number of pairs is 5, not 10.

questions.explanation: n = 5 pairs, each with two orientations at metaphase I: 2^5 = 32.

questions.stem: A molecule makes the inner mitochondrial membrane leaky to protons. What is the effect?

options.text: Energy from electron transport is released as heat instead of making ATP
options.why: Correct. The gradient dissipates without passing through ATP synthase.
Electron transport can continue.
Glycolysis is unaffected directly.
The gradient is lost.

questions.explanation: The gradient dissipates without passing through ATP synthase.

questions.stem: Why can yeast continue to make some ATP without oxygen?

options.why: Yeast is not photosynthetic.

options.text: Fermentation regenerates NAD⁺ so glycolysis can continue
options.why: Correct. Glycolysis needs NAD⁺ to keep running.

options.text: Fermentation produces more ATP than respiration
options.why: It produces far less.

options.text: The Krebs cycle runs without oxygen
options.why: It depends on NAD⁺ from the electron transport chain.

questions.explanation: Glycolysis needs NAD⁺ to keep running.

questions.stem: Which feature is shared by all living organisms, supporting common ancestry?

options.why: These are eukaryotic features.
Prokaryotes lack a nucleus.
Only plants and algae have them.

questions.explanation: All organisms read codons the same way.

questions.stem: An inhibitor reduces an enzyme's rate, but adding a large amount of substrate restores the maximum rate. What kind of inhibitor is it?

options.why: Extra substrate cannot overcome allosteric inhibition.
Denaturation is not reversed by substrate.
Cofactors help enzymes work.
Correct. Excess substrate outcompetes an inhibitor for the active site.

questions.explanation: Excess substrate outcompetes an inhibitor for the active site.

questions.stem: Which change would most likely disrupt the tertiary structure of a protein?

options.text: A change in pH that alters the charges on R groups

options.text: Breaking a covalent bond within the sugar-phosphate backbone
options.why: That is in nucleic acids, not proteins.

questions.explanation: Tertiary structure depends on R-group interactions, including ionic bonds.

questions.stem: Which is an example of positive feedback?

options.why: That is negative feedback.
That is negative feedback.

options.text: Oxytocin increases contractions during childbirth, which causes more oxytocin release
options.why: Correct. The response amplifies the stimulus.
That is negative feedback.

questions.explanation: The response amplifies the stimulus.

questions.stem: A cell secretes large amounts of a digestive enzyme. Which organelles would be most abundant?

questions.stem: A point mutation changes the mRNA codon GAA to UAA. Which type of mutation is this?

rubric.criterion: A valid controlled variable.
rubric.example: Temperature, enzyme concentration, substrate concentration or volume.

parts.prompt: Calculate the percent change in reaction rate when the pH changes from 7 to 5.

rubric.criterion: Correct calculation.

parts.prompt: Explain why the reaction rate is low at pH 3 and pH 11.

rubric.criterion: Extreme pH changes the charges on amino acid R groups.
rubric.example: H⁺ concentration alters ionic and hydrogen bonds that hold the enzyme's shape.

rubric.criterion: The active site's shape changes (denaturation), so substrate binds poorly.
rubric.example: Fewer enzyme–substrate complexes form, lowering the rate.

parts.prompt: The student repeats the experiment at pH 7 with twice as much enzyme and the same amount of substrate. Predict the effect on the initial rate, and justify your prediction.

rubric.criterion: Predicts the initial rate increases.
rubric.example: Higher than 48 µmol/min, up to about double.

rubric.criterion: Justifies with more active sites available when substrate is plentiful.
rubric.example: More enzyme molecules can bind substrate at the same time.

parts.prompt: A competitive inhibitor is added to the reaction at the optimal pH. Describe how increasing the substrate concentration would affect the inhibition, and explain why.

rubric.criterion: Inhibition decreases at high substrate concentration.
rubric.example: The rate approaches the uninhibited maximum.

rubric.criterion: Explains competition for the active site.
rubric.example: Substrate molecules outcompete the inhibitor for the active site.

parts.prompt: Describe how you would construct an appropriate graph of the data: the type of graph, the axes and their labels, and the scale.

rubric.criterion: Line or scatter graph with time on the x-axis.
rubric.example: Day on the x-axis, population size on the y-axis.

rubric.criterion: Axes labeled with units and linear scales; points plotted accurately and connected.
rubric.example: y-axis from 0 to at least 600.

parts.prompt: Calculate the average rate of population growth between day 4 and day 8.

rubric.criterion: Correct calculation with units.
rubric.example: (563 − 232) ÷ 4 = 82.75 individuals per day

parts.prompt: Identify the type of population growth shown and estimate the carrying capacity.

rubric.criterion: Logistic growth.
rubric.example: An S-shaped curve that levels off.

rubric.criterion: Carrying capacity estimate consistent with the data.
rubric.example: About 600.

parts.prompt: Explain why the growth rate decreases as the population approaches the carrying capacity.

rubric.criterion: Identifies a density-dependent factor.
rubric.example: Competition for limited food and space, or buildup of wastes.

rubric.criterion: Links it to lower birth rates or higher death rates.
rubric.example: As density rises, fewer resources per individual reduce reproduction and survival.

parts.prompt: The researchers repeat the experiment with double the food supply. Predict the effect on the carrying capacity and justify your prediction.

rubric.criterion: Predicts a higher carrying capacity.
rubric.example: Greater than about 600.

rubric.criterion: Justifies: food was a limiting resource.
rubric.example: More resources allow the environment to support more individuals.

parts.prompt: Identify an appropriate control for the experiment, and explain why the students measured percent change rather than change in mass.

rubric.criterion: The 0 M (distilled water) treatment, or cores with no solution change.
rubric.example: Distilled water.

rubric.criterion: Percent change allows comparison of cores with slightly different starting masses.
rubric.example: It standardizes for initial mass.

parts.prompt: Estimate the sucrose concentration that is isotonic to the potato cells, and calculate the solute potential of that solution (Ψs = −iCRT, R = 0.0831, T in kelvins).

rubric.criterion: Isotonic concentration where the change in mass is zero.
rubric.example: About 0.25 M, interpolating between 0.2 and 0.4 M.

rubric.criterion: Solute potential calculated correctly from the estimate.

parts.prompt: Explain the change in mass of the cores in the 0.8 M solution.

rubric.criterion: Water moved out of the cells by osmosis toward the lower water potential of the solution.
rubric.example: The solution is hypertonic, so the cells lost water and mass.

parts.prompt: Describe the role of cAMP in this pathway.

rubric.criterion: cAMP is a second messenger that relays and amplifies the signal inside the cell.
rubric.example: It activates protein kinase A.

parts.prompt: Explain how a single epinephrine molecule can cause the release of a large number of glucose molecules.

rubric.criterion: Amplification: each activated enzyme activates many molecules at the next step.
rubric.example: One adenylyl cyclase makes many cAMP; each kinase phosphorylates many targets.

parts.prompt: A mutation alters the enzyme that breaks down cAMP, so that it is inactive. Predict the effect on glycogen breakdown, and justify your prediction.

rubric.criterion: Correct prediction.
rubric.example: Glycogen breakdown continues longer than normal after the signal ends.

rubric.criterion: Justification using the pathway.
rubric.example: CAMP remains high, keeping protein kinase A active.

parts.prompt: Calculate the frequency of the b allele and the expected number of heterozygous beetles.

rubric.criterion: q from the recessive phenotype frequency.
Expected heterozygotes.

parts.prompt: Identify two conditions that must be met for the population to remain in Hardy–Weinberg equilibrium.

rubric.criterion: Two correct conditions.
rubric.example: A large population, random mating, no mutation, no migration, no natural selection.

parts.prompt: Birds that prey on the beetles find beetles with green shells more easily on the new background. Predict how the frequency of the b allele will change over several generations, and justify your prediction.

rubric.criterion: Predicts q increases.
rubric.example: Beetles with brown shells (bb) survive and reproduce more.

rubric.criterion: Justifies with differential survival and reproduction.
rubric.example: Selection removes B alleles faster, because both BB and Bb beetles are eaten more.

parts.prompt: State the null hypothesis, and calculate the expected number of offspring in each category.

rubric.criterion: Null hypothesis: the genes assort independently, giving a 9 : 3 : 3 : 1 ratio.
rubric.example: Any differences are due to chance.

rubric.criterion: Expected counts.

parts.prompt: Calculate the chi-square value and determine whether to reject the null hypothesis at p = 0.05 (critical value 7.81 for 3 degrees of freedom).

rubric.criterion: Correct chi-square value.
Correct conclusion with comparison to the critical value.
rubric.example: 110.79 is greater than 7.81, so reject the null hypothesis.

parts.prompt: Propose an explanation for the results.

rubric.criterion: Explanation consistent with the conclusion.
rubric.example: The genes are likely linked on the same chromosome, so parental combinations are inherited together more often.
